title: Kingdom of Lindsey
capsule: Lindsey was an early Anglo-Saxon kingdom occupying the limestone ridge and fenland margins between the Humber estuary and The Wash, with Lincoln (Roman Lindum Colonia) as its probable capital. Its royal genealogy, tracing lineage back through Woden to the historical figure Winta, survives in the Anglian Collection but no ruler can be securely dated, making the kingdom one of the most obscure of the Heptarchy. Lindsey changed hands repeatedly between Northumbria and Mercia throughout the seventh century, serving primarily as a buffer zone whose territorial control signalled the balance of power between those two larger kingdoms. By the late seventh century it had lost effective independence, becoming a sub-kingdom under Mercian overlordship before absorption into the Danelaw.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Lindsey's territorial core is inferred from later ecclesiastical and county boundaries; no contemporary documents delimit it, and even the dates of individual reigns are speculative reconstructions from genealogical king lists.
